title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos using the likeness of a real, named immigration attorney to advertise fraudulent legal services to immigrants. This is an impersonation failure in the social media distribution layer, not inside any law firm or legal platform. The AI was used as a production tool by bad actors to generate convincing video content at scale, lowering the cost of identity fraud far enough to sustain thousands of fake profiles simultaneously.

The failure became visible only after victims began contacting the real attorney's office, meaning no platform-side detection caught it before harm reached real people. Catching it earlier would have required either automated detection of synthetic media impersonating known individuals or active monitoring by the platforms where the content appeared. The scale of removal, nearly 6,500 profiles across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram, indicates the content persisted long enough to spread widely before any coordinated takedown began.

It is not established that any victim successfully recovered money paid, that law enforcement has identified or charged anyone, or that the platforms had prior notice of this specific campaign before the attorney and his anti-piracy contractor acted.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence scam targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos featuring Leal's likeness, offering fraudulent immigration services such as US residency assistance for $2,200. The scams typically direct potential victims through social media videos to contact numbers via WhatsApp, where scammers send fake contracts and request payment through apps like Venmo and Zelle. Leal first discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office about services he never offered.

The fraud has escalated dramatically over the past three months, prompting Leal to hire an anti-piracy company to combat it. So far, the company has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across multiple platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The situation has forced Leal to change his personal phone number. He plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to launch an investigation and is warning immigrants to verify the identities of anyone offering legal services online and to be suspicious of payment requests through digital transfer apps.
